artifacts.summary: Root-causes and experimentally-verified fixes for both remaining red suites (missing task-lookup-lib.sh in test-postflight-deploy-gate.sh's REQUIRED_LIBS; a false-positive in lint-json-channel-discipline.sh's check_emit_perline redirect exclusion), plus a full item-(d) audit finding two more fixtures (test-handoff-dispatch-identity.sh, test-git-commit-scoped.sh) with the same missing-lib gap, both currently dormant rather than red.

memory_candidates.content: In agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/tests/, a fixture that copies task-lock.sh (or any script with an unconditional `source lib/X.sh`, no `[ -f ]` guard) via an explicit REQUIRED_LIBS-style array must include every lib that unconditionally-sourced script itself sources, or the fixture silently breaks even if the missing lib is unrelated to what the test is actually exercising. Contrast with skill-base.sh's soft-guarded sourcing of the same lib (`if [ -f ... ]; then source; else WARNING fallback; fi`), which degrades gracefully instead. When auditing for this class of gap, check not just whether a suite is currently red, but whether a --dry-run flag or similar is masking a code path that would otherwise execute the unconditionally-sourced script.

lint-json-channel-discipline.sh's check_emit_perline() heuristic (per-line EMIT direction) excludes only >&2, >&3, and $(...)-captured lines when collecting stdout-write candidates -- it does not recognize a generic `> "$var"` file redirect, causing a false-positive VIOLATION on any line that writes to a temp file via a variable-named path. Fix: add `grep -vE '>[[:space:]]*"?\$\{?[A-Za-z_]'` to the exclusion pipeline (scoped to variable-named redirect targets, conservative by design). Verified this does not weaken detection of genuine multi-write violations.
